source.description: Where the number comes from, e.g. measured or estimated.

agents.description: The agents on this account (AgentView.account): running on it, or at rest with their prompt cache alive. One past its cache life is on none.

machines.description: The machines this account is logged in on, as node ids (node.status `id`): this daemon's own when its login here is good, then each runner whose last heartbeat names it logged in, by id.

label.description: The name screens show; the account's own name until an alias is set.

vendor.description: The tool the account is for (`claude`, `opencode`, ...), as account.add set it.

recover.description: Whether a dead usage read may spend one real turn to fix itself (hl account recover).

paused.description: Paused by the founder (account.set paused): no agent starts on it, and its agents move off at their next turn when another account has room. Absent: not paused.

email.description: The Anthropic account's email, kept from its last login so it shows after the login drops; null when none was kept. Given to the founder's app only, never to an agent.

end_is_default.description: No end day is typed: end is null, and the account ends only when its login drops.

agents_assigned.description: Only with accounts.list `roster: true`. Agents on this account (Account.agents), running or at rest with their prompt cache alive (the figure `hl account list` prints).

agents_running.description: Only with accounts.list `roster: true`. Agents mid-turn on this account.

agents_background.description: Only with accounts.list `roster: true`, and absent when the daemon runs no supervisor. Agents on this account at their prompt whose session still runs background work; never in agents_running.

agents_unplaced.description: Only with accounts.list `roster: true`. Agents whose config cannot be read and so count on no account; the same on every account, and every figure above is a floor while it is above 0.

reason.description: Why the login ended failed, one plain line (e.g. logged in to an Anthropic account other than the one recorded for this account); absent unless it failed.

login.description: The login in progress or the last one to end; null when none was started. Reported on the accounts topic as account.changed. Never carries the authorize URL: only the founder's account.login reply has it.

plan.description: Only with accounts.list `usage: true`. The plan as Anthropic names it (`Ultra`, `Max`, `Pro`), from the subscription and rate-limit tier claude reports; null when not recorded.

windows.description: Only with accounts.list `usage: true`. The shortest and, when the vendor has one, the longest window: the figure read, the one that may be acted on, and where it came from.

effective.description: The figure the daemon acts on.

source.description: Where the figure comes from, or why it is not trusted.

ctx_pct.description: Only with accounts.list `usage: true`. Context used by the account's last session, percent.

age_s.description: Only with accounts.list `usage: true`. Seconds since the usage was read.

runway.description: Only with accounts.list `usage: true`. How long the account lasts at its recent burn, in words (`~10m to wall`), as `hl account list` prints it.

assignable.description: Only with accounts.list `usage: true`. Whether one more agent may start on it.

assign_reason.description: Only with accounts.list `usage: true`. Why assignable is what it is.

kind.description: What keeps new work off it: its subscription end day has passed, the founder paused it, its weekly or 5-hour window is at the wall, it is not logged in (which wins over the rest), it may take work but another account fits a new start better, or something else (a stale, lost or unreadable reading).

text.description: The daemon's reason in words, as `hl status` prints it. An ended account that is logged in with a fresh reading adds that its end day may be out of date.

not_picked.description: Only with accounts.list `usage: true`. Why the daemon's pick for its vendor would not choose it now; null while it is a candidate. When the pick chooses none, a start may still fall back to a refused account. assign_reason says whether one more agent may start on it; not_picked says why the pick passes it over. A client shows not_picked.

reason.description: The line a row shows beside STALLED, as an agent's stall does: `login expired` for authentication_failed, else the error itself.

error.description: The StopFailure error that stalled it, as the CLI gave it.

detail.description: The turn that showed it, in words.

stalled.description: Set while the account is STALLED: a turn on it ended on an error that says the account itself cannot be used (a refused login, an org that disallows it, a hold or billing problem), or on one error the daemon does not name four times with no good turn between. No agent is placed on it; account.wake, a login or a good turn there ends it. null while it is usable. Absent from a daemon that does not send it.

state.description: behind: used_pct is at or under line_pct. ahead: over the line by at most pace_burst_pct points. over: further ahead. The pace holds no start.

line_pct.description: Where the line is now: pace_target_pct x (now - start) / (end - start), where start is its weekly reset less 7 days and end is that reset or the subscription end, whichever comes first.

used_pct.description: The weekly window's used percent the pace is judged on: the last weekly reading, kept until its reset.

rate_pct_h.description: Points of the week per hour the account may use from now to reach pace_target_pct at the end of its week: (pace_target_pct - used_pct) / hours left; 0 at or past the target.

pace.description: Only with accounts.list `usage: true`. The account's weekly pace (settings pace_target_pct, pace_burst_pct), shown only: it holds no start. Judged on its last weekly reading, which is kept until its weekly reset even when it is stale. null when it has no weekly reading or its reset is not known.

usd_per_pct.description: API-equivalent dollars per point of the window; 0 when source is none.

source.description: own: the median of the account's own recent stretches. pooled: the median of every account's, in Pro units, times plan_scale. none: no account has a stretch yet.

samples.description: The account's own stretches; it switches to own at 5.

short.description: Dollars per point of the 5-hour window.

usd_per_pct.description: API-equivalent dollars per point of the window; 0 when source is none.

source.description: own: the median of the account's own recent stretches. pooled: the median of every account's, in Pro units, times plan_scale. none: no account has a stretch yet.

samples.description: The account's own stretches; it switches to own at 5.

long.description: Dollars per point of the week.

plan_scale.description: The plan's size relative to Pro (Pro 1, Max 5x 5, Max 20x 20), from the recorded subscription type and rate-limit tier.

factors.description: Only with accounts.list `usage: true`. What a point of each window costs on this account in API-equivalent dollars, learned from stretches of live readings over which the figure rose 5 points or more: the account's priced token calls in the stretch over the rise. Recomputed every 10 minutes from the last 7 days. null before the daemon has read the account.

your_wait_s.description: The median seconds from a turn put on a person to that person giving it back, over turns given back in the window; null when none was.

use.description: Each agent's use of each account on each machine in the window, largest cost first; an agent on two accounts or two machines has a row for each.

AgentAccountUse.description: One agent's use of one account on one machine. tokens and cost are measured; week_pct is an estimate of the split, not of the account's rise.

agent.description: Empty for the calls of no agent's worktree (the founder's own sessions, the usage poll); drawn as Other.

node.description: The machine that spent the calls, as a node id (node.status `id`); calls kept from before machines were recorded count as this daemon's. An agent that spent on two machines has a row on each.

share.description: This row's cost over the account's cost in the window, 0 to 1.

oneOf.description: Estimated points of the account's weekly limit used: share times the account's rise in the window, so an account's rows add up to it.

week_pct.description: null when the account has no reading in the window or its calls had no list price.

accounts.description: How many accounts have a reading.

oneOf.description: Percent of the week left, averaged over the accounts that have a reading at that time, each weighed by its weekly plan budget as budget.left_pct is (alike when no account has one); an account that could not be used then (its login gone or expired) counts as 0.

past.description: What usage samples recorded, oldest first.

oneOf.description: Percent of the week left, averaged over the accounts that have a reading at that time, each weighed by its weekly plan budget as budget.left_pct is (alike when no account has one); an account that could not be used then (its login gone or expired) counts as 0.

future.description: A guess. Each account's week goes at its pace since that week began. A week that resets starts again from nothing used. An account whose last reading is stale or at a wall keeps that reading until its reset and is not left out. An account that cannot be used now (its login gone or expired) counts as 0 ahead. Kept apart from `past`, never joined to it.

oneOf.description: How long its headroom lasts at the current burn, whichever window runs out first; null when its reading is stale, there is no burn, or the window resets first.

node.description: The machine that spent the calls, as a node id (node.status `id`); calls kept from before machines were recorded count as this daemon's. An agent that spent on two machines has a row on each. null on the (unattributed) row of plan money with no priced call, which this daemon's own (unattributed) row takes instead when there is one.

tokens.description: Tokens the agent used in the span.

cost.description: Its cost in US dollars at list price in the span, from the token log.

share.description: Its cost as a fraction (0 to 1) of everyone's cost in the span; 0 when nothing was spent.

fracs.description: Its cost share of each account in the span, by account name (a fraction, 0 to 1). An account on which nothing at all was spent is absent; one on which others spent but none of this agent's tokens was priced is 0.

plan_cost.description: Its plan money in the span, US dollars: each account's week rise in the span times that account's weekly budget, split by its cost share of that account (`fracs`). Token prices only split it; they never size it.

agent_use.description: What each agent used on each machine over the last `range` (the span of `past`), largest cost first, ties by name then machine; plan money of a week's rise with no priced call comes last as a row of (unattributed) with no tokens. Absent from a daemon that does not send it.

overlay.description: Only with `agent`: the points of the combined week the pick had used by each time of `past`, one number per `past` entry in the same order: its cost share of each account times what that account had used so far, averaged over the accounts as `past` is. Empty when the pick used nothing in the span or is not an agent or group. Absent from a daemon that does not send it.

oneOf.description: What the 5h window had left, in percent; null where it had no reading.
What the weekly window had left, in percent; null where it had no reading.
What the week would have left on the pace line at that time (100 - line_pct); null where its reset is not known or pacing is off.

past.description: What usage samples recorded, at the same points as `past`.

oneOf.description: What the 5h window had left, in percent; null where it had no reading.
What the weekly window had left, in percent; null where it had no reading.
What the week would have left on the pace line at that time (100 - line_pct); null where its reset is not known or pacing is off.

future.description: The guess of `future` for this account, at the same points: the week at its pace since it began, the 5h window at its use over the last day, starting again from nothing at each reset, so its line is a saw.

unused_pct.description: Only on a weekly (7d) reset the samples recorded: the percent of that week left unused at the last sample before it. Absent for a 5h reset, a guessed one, or a week with no sample.

resets.description: Resets in the span, oldest first: those samples recorded, then those guessed.

five_hour.description: Whether its readings carry a 5-hour figure. One with none (a verified Ultra has no 5-hour limit) has five_left null everywhere, no 5h resets and no five_runs_out_at.

unused_pct.description: Percent of the week guessed left unused at `at`, going at its pace since the week began.

unused_usd.description: That share of its weekly plan budget (budget.accounts[].week_usd), US dollars; null for an account with no budget here (unmetered, or no longer listed).

forecast.description: What its week is guessed to leave unused at its next reset (the one after, when the reset passed since its last reading); null when no reset is known, its last reading is older than two hours, it cannot be used now, or it ends before it.

five_runs_out_at.description: When its 5-hour window runs out at its use over the last day, counted on from its last reading; null when it lasts to its reset, is not in use, its reading is stale, or it has no 5-hour window.

by_account.description: Each account that has a reading in the span, by name: its windows and its pace line, for a chart per account. Absent from a daemon that does not send it.

plan.description: The plan as Anthropic names it (Pro, Max, Ultra); null when none is recorded.

fee_usd.description: Its monthly fee in US dollars: the one set on the account (account.set plan_fee), else its plan's listed one (Pro 20, Max 100, Ultra 200); 0 for a plan with none.

used_pct.description: Percent of its week used now; null with no reading. A week whose reset has passed is 0.

spent_usd.description: used_pct of week_usd; null with no reading.

left_usd.description: week_usd less spent_usd; null with no reading.

five_hour.description: Whether its reading carries a 5-hour figure: an Ultra account has no 5-hour limit, so none.

extra.description: Its extra usage; null when its last reading named none (unknown, never zero).

week_usd.description: The weekly budgets together, of the accounts with a fee and a reading.

spent_usd.description: What those accounts spent of them this week.

left_pct.description: Percent of week_usd left: the accounts' weeks weighted by their budgets, not averaged. null when no account counts.

extra_spent.description: Extra usage spent this billing month by the accounts whose reading names an amount, per currency (USD: dollars). Never part of spent_usd.

budget.description: The week in plan money: each account's monthly fee turned into a weekly budget, of which its week's percent used is spent. Absent from a daemon that does not send it.

Retro.description: The cost of one founder's task: its wall time, and the tokens spent inside the doing windows of every task in its subtree, per agent.

wall_seconds.description: From the task's creation to its done or discard time; to now while it is open.

tokens.description: All agents together: inp, cc, cr and out (thinking is a part of out).

cost.description: USD at list price, all agents together.

agents.description: One row per agent that was doing a task of the subtree, most tokens first, ties by agent.

doing_seconds.description: Time it held tasks of the subtree in doing, waits on a blocker included.

tasks.description: The subtree tasks it did, by id.

agents.description: List-price cost in US dollars of each agent that day.

DayCosts.description: What the agents cost per local calendar day, oldest first; a day with no calls is absent.

agents.description: Plan money in US dollars of each agent that day: each account's week rises seen that day (dated by the reading that shows them) times its weekly budget, split by the agents' list-price cost on that account that day; money of a rise with no priced call is under (unattributed).

extra.description: Extra usage spent that day, per currency: the rise of each account's spent between its readings, dated by the later one; a drop is its billing month starting over, counted from 0.

PlanDayCosts.description: The plan money the agents used per local calendar day of the range, oldest first; a day nothing rose and no extra usage was spent is absent. Absent from a daemon that does not send it.

on.description: Whether extra usage is turned on: the account may keep working past its limits, paid on top of its plan.

cap.description: Its monthly cap, in major units of currency; null when none is named.

spent.description: What it spent this billing month, in major units of currency; null when none is named.

currency.description: The currency the amounts are in (USD); null when none is named.

ExtraUsage.description: An account's extra usage as its last reading named it: money paid on top of the plan in its billing month. It never enters the plan money.

methods.name: accounts.list
methods.summary: Accounts with login state, use, agents, recent moves.

schema.description: Add each account's agents_assigned, agents_running, agents_background and agents_unplaced. Default false.
Add each account's plan, windows, ctx_pct, age_s, runway, assignable and assign_reason (what `hl account list` prints beside the windows), pace and not_picked. Default false.

methods.name: account.set
methods.summary: The account Settings form in one call: alias, usage recovery, the month cycle, the plan fee and pause; nothing is written if any is refused.

schema.description: Alias, one plain line; empty clears.
The one-month subscription switch (hl account cycle on|off); off keeps the end day.
Last usable day YYYY-MM-DD; a date alone turns the cycle on, as `hl account cycle --end` does; null clears it.
The account's monthly fee in US dollars when it is not its plan's listed one; null goes back to the plan's.

methods.description: Fields not given are left alone. Chosen over set_cycle_on/set_cycle_end methods because the UI saves these together and the CLI twins (cycle, recover, alias) each write one of these fields.

methods.name: account.wake
methods.summary: Wake a STALLED account: its stall ends, agents may be placed on it again and the agents stalled with it are released, as session.wake clears a stalled agent (hl account wake). A login on the account, or a turn that ends well there, ends the stall too. Refused (gate state) when the account is not stalled.

methods.name: account.read_usage
methods.summary: Read the account's usage again now: Accepted at once, and the usage poll reads the account first at its next tick, past its cadence. accounts.list shows the reading once it lands. Asking again before that read ends is the same ask. A failed read is backed off as a polled one is, and spends no real turn while backed off. Refused (gate state) when the account is not logged in or STALLED, or its vendor has no limits to read.

methods.name: account.add
methods.summary: Register an account on this machine; it is not logged in until account.login runs.

schema.description: The new account's name: one plain line, no slash, not starting with a dot. Omitted: account<n>, n the number of accounts plus one, skipping a name in use.
The tool the account is for: claude, codex, or another the daemon has a driver for; omitted means claude.

methods.description: As `hl account add <name> --no-login`: the account's directory is made and linked to the shared files, and nothing is logged in, so accounts.list shows it with login_state needs_login and the accounts topic sends account.changed. A name already used is refused (gate `state`). A name that is empty, holds a slash, starts with a dot or would not be read back as text is bad_request, field `account`; a vendor the daemon has no driver for is bad_request, field `vendor`. Nothing is changed on a refusal. The app then calls account.login. Offering to trust the agents' worktrees on the new account is not part of it (settings.trust).

methods.name: account.login
methods.summary: Start a login on the account; answers the login id, the URL to open and, for codex, the code to type there.

url.description: Claude: the authorize URL the CLI printed; the person opens it and brings the code back with account.login_code. Codex: the device page; the person opens it and types device_code there, and nothing comes back.

device_code.description: Codex only: the one-time code the CLI printed, for the person to type at url. Absent for claude. Kept in memory for the login only: never in an event, a log, the login row or the kept reply a retry gets.

methods.description: No terminal is opened: the CLI runs without one, its URL is read from its stdout and its code is fed to its stdin by account.login_code. Refused with gate `state` while the account is already logging in; not_found for an unknown account. The end of a login is not a method: the accounts topic reports it in the account's `login`, state waiting, then code_sent after account.login_code, then done, or failed with a `reason`, or cancelled by account.login_cancel. A login that is done leaves login_state ok. A codex login (codex login --device-auth) goes from waiting straight to done or failed when the CLI exits, with no code_sent: account.login_code on it is refused, gate `state`.

methods.name: account.login_cancel
methods.description: Idempotent: a login already ended answers accepted. An id the daemon never issued is not_found. The login's whole process group is killed, since the CLI ignores SIGTERM for a second.

methods.name: account.login_code
methods.summary: Hand the one-time code from the authorize page to a login waiting for it.

schema.description: One-time; written to the CLI's stdin and nowhere else.

methods.description: The code is never echoed back, never in an event, a log or the request record. Refused with gate `state` when the login is not waiting for a code. An id the daemon never issued is not_found. A codex login never waits for a code, so it is always refused there.

methods.name: accounts.discover
methods.summary: Logins already on this Mac, outside Handline, that an account could use: ~/.claude and ~/.codex.

source.description: The folder the login lives in, as ~/.codex; what account.adopt takes.

logged_in.description: Whether the vendor's own check says it is logged in; null when it cannot be told.

adoptable.description: Whether account.adopt takes it: true for codex. A Claude login is keyed by its config folder, so a client shows it as found and the account logs in again.

found.description: One row per folder that exists, claude first; empty when there is none.

methods.description: Read from each vendor's own login check only (claude auth status, codex login status, under that folder): never a credential's content. Owner only.

methods.name: account.adopt
methods.summary: Make a codex account that uses a codex login already on this Mac (accounts.discover).

schema.description: codex. Any other is bad_request, field vendor: a Claude login cannot be shared, so the account is added and logs in.
A source accounts.discover answered for that vendor. Another is not_found, what source.
The new account's name, as account.add takes it; omitted: account<n>.

methods.description: The account gets its own config folder with only auth.json linked to the source's, so its hooks, instructions and sessions stay out of the person's own folder; it starts logged in as the same login (login_state ok) and the accounts topic sends account.changed. While the link holds, a logout in either logs both out, which a client says before the call; a token refresh that rewrites the file can make the two drift apart, and the account then logs in on its own. Refused, gate `state`, when the source is not logged in or the name is in use; a bad name is bad_request, field account. Nothing is changed on a refusal.

methods.name: account.remove
methods.summary: Log an account out and take it off the roster; dry_run names what would happen.

schema.description: Change nothing: answer `plan` and `would_remove`. A dry run needs no `confirm`.
The account's name, as the founder typed it; required unless dry_run.

would_remove.description: Dry run only: whether the removal would go ahead.

plan.description: Dry run only: what it would do, line by line, or the one line that says why it would refuse.

methods.description: The sequence of `hl account remove`: refused (gate `state`) while an agent is on the account or when claude's logout fails. The account's directory is moved aside, never deleted. A dry run writes nothing and records nothing.

methods.name: stats.get
methods.summary: Counts over a window, and each agent's use of each account's weekly limit.

methods.name: stats.outlook
methods.summary: The week left of the accounts together, recorded and guessed, each account's runway, and what the agents cost per day.

schema.description: Headroom: that long back and as long ahead. Cost per day: the last that many days (under 1 day counts as 1).

Also give `overlay` for this pick: an agent, the key of a row of the agents table a client draws. It rides on this call and not on a method of its own because the curve is read against `past` and must be sampled at the same moment as it; one pick costs one array, not one per agent.

methods.name: stats.retro
methods.summary: What a founder's task cost: wall time, and tokens per agent from the doing windows of its subtree.
methods.description: A read only. The subtree is the task and every task opened under it, to any depth. A doing window of a task runs from the moment its holder began it (task_begin or task_start, or a delivery of it landing with the holder) to the first of: done, discard, release, a report, any other move out of doing, handoff to another agent, or the holder beginning another task. A holder has at most one open window, so its windows never overlap; doing_seconds is time the agent held the task in doing, waits on a blocker included. A call of token_calls counts to an agent when its ts is after a window's begin and up to its end (as in stats.get) in one of that agent's windows and its cwd is in that agent's worktree. Calls outside every window are not counted. A task that is not found is `not_found`; a task that is not a founder's task (its reporter is not human) is `bad_request`.
